macro.summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +6.2%; weakest: Lean hogs -22.8%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.85% (-15 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +24 bp (-8 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.16% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.72 (+1.4% in a month, +5.5% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.767 (+7.3% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.651 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 19.67 (+6.0%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -6.4% in a month (+4.9% YTD); VIX 26.8. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 84.67 $/bbl (-13.7% in a month), Brent 91.29, ULSD 3.677 $/gal (-18.7%), natural gas 3.62 (+4.4%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -19.0% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.7%, Hang Seng -3.5%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 9 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (27%); S&P GSCI -14.2% in a month; gold -12.6%.

macro.caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.

us_econ: Jobs: payrolls +165k in 2026-10 (3-month average +137k), unemployment 4.1% (-0.1), wages 3.1% y/y. Growth: real GDP 4.3% annualized in 2026-Q3, consumer spending 4.2%. Policy: fed funds target 3.75-4.0% (effective 3.88%); 2-year Treasury 4.61% (+0.73 vs fed funds: market pricing hikes); 10-year breakeven inflation 2.12%, real 10-year 2.73%. Farm prices (PPI farm products) +2.6% y/y. For ags: high real yields and a firm dollar weigh on fund demand for commodities; sticky inflation keeps rates high (carry and storage costs up); a weak job market or falling real incomes hits meat and dairy demand first.

energy.read: Gas storage 3,858 Bcf (week to 2026-11-20), -24 Bcf vs a 5-year average -29 for the week; +103 Bcf (+2.7%) vs the 5-year average, -66 vs last year. Crude stocks 418.9 mb (+1.1 mb on the week, -2.9% vs 5-yr avg); gasoline +5.2 mb, distillate +1.6 mb; refinery utilization 97.5%. 3-2-1 crack $35.08/bbl (ULSD $69.89, gasoline $17.68). NG weather/positioning: squeeze risk ELEVATED (2 of 7 cold-risk checks on; managed money net -211,476 (2nd pct of 3 yrs, -54,628 in 4 wks)). GEFS AO week 2 -1.00 (now -0.28); GEFS PNA week 2 +0.56 (western ridge / eastern trough). Cold-pattern signals are present but the models have not turned colder yet. Keep shorts small and in options; switch to HIGH if the 2-3 day trend or weeks 3-4 turn cold. Options: NG IV 83% vs RV 67%; CL IV 47% vs RV 53%; HO IV 50% vs RV 49%; RB IV 44% vs RV 43%. For ags: diesel and natural gas set farm fuel, drying and nitrogen fertilizer costs; crude and gasoline drive ethanol and biodiesel margins (corn, soybean oil).
